items.headline: Historic commission agenda: 1,200 sq ft ADU at 1391 Washington Street
items.summary: The November 5 Historical & Landmarks Commission agenda listed a public hearing on a recommendation for a 1,200-square-foot detached accessory dwelling unit and a 347-square-foot detached garage at 1391 Washington Street, a property on the Historic Resource Inventory. The project (PLN26-00020) needs a Significant Property Alteration / Architectural Review and is listed as categorically exempt from CEQA.

items.headline: Historic commission to pick member for preservation ordinance consultant panel
items.summary: The November 5 Historical & Landmarks Commission agenda listed selecting one commissioner to serve on the review board choosing a consultant for the city's Historic Preservation Ordinance update.

items.headline: Sunnyvale historic context update to cover Asian American and minority contributions
items.summary: The Heritage Preservation Commission's November 4 agenda listed a draft update to the city's Historical Context Statement to include contributions by Asian Americans and other minority groups, a Council priority project. The same agenda included a presentation on recent changes to SB 9 (including SB 450 and AB 1061) affecting two-unit developments and urban lot splits in single-family zones.

items.headline: Technology Park plan has fewer homes than zoning allowed, but traffic concerns remain
items.summary: The applicant said current zoning would allow roughly 468 to 620 units, and over 1,200 with a state density bonus, versus the 290 approved. Staff's traffic analysis estimated 1,368 net new daily trips and 2 more vehicles in an existing 30-car queue at Curtner/White Oaks/Camden. The only required mitigation was a mid-block crosswalk and related pedestrian upgrades on Campbell Technology Park. Several council members and neighbors raised concerns about congestion and about removing redwoods along the Paseo de Palomas fence line.

items.headline: Council renews $175,000 police recruitment contract; applications up from 57 to 355
items.summary: On November 2, the council approved a one-year contract with All Star Talent for online police recruitment, skipping competitive bidding. The department said applications rose from about 57 in 2022 to 355 last year, with 11 officers hired and through probation since 2023. Vice Mayor Bybee voted yes but questioned whether the program favors quantity over quality.

items.headline: Council agenda: $11.8 million for Finch Avenue property purchase
items.summary: The November 2 City Council agenda listed a budget modification adding $11,825,000 to the Parkland Dedication Fund to buy the Finch Property at 10480 Finch Avenue. The item sat on the consent calendar, which is normally approved in a single motion.

items.headline: Council agenda: grant and design contract for McClellan Road Bridge
items.summary: The November 2 agenda listed a resolution to accept $850,000 in Caltrans-administered grant funds for the McClellan Road Bridge Project. It also listed a design services agreement with Biggs Cardosa Associates, Inc. for up to $1,278,700.

items.headline: Council agenda: study session on updating 2019 Emergency Operations Plan
items.summary: The November 2 agenda listed a study session on proposed updates to Cupertino's 2019 Emergency Operations Plan, the city's framework for responding to disasters and other emergencies.
